questions.question: Which of the following is the correct syntax for an if statement in Python that prints 'Hello' if x is greater than 0?

What will be the output of the following code if x is set to 5?

x = 5
if x > 3:
    print("Greater")
Which of the following examples correctly demonstrates the proper syntax for an if-else statement in Python?
options: if x == 10: print("Ten") else: print("Not Ten")
if x == 10 then print("Ten") else print("Not Ten")
if x == 10 { print("Ten") } else { print("Not Ten") }
questions.correct_answer: if x == 10: print("Ten") else: print("Not Ten")

questions.question: Which of the following if-statement examples correctly uses the 'elif' clause in Python?
options: if x < 10: print("Less than 10") elif x == 10: print("Equal to 10") else: print("Greater than 10")
if x < 10 then print("Less than 10") elif x == 10 then print("Equal to 10") else print("Greater than 10")
if x < 10: print("Less than 10"); elif x == 10: print("Equal to 10"); else: print("Greater than 10")
if (x < 10) print("Less than 10") elif (x == 10) print("Equal to 10") else print("Greater than 10")
questions.correct_answer: if x < 10: print("Less than 10") elif x == 10: print("Equal to 10") else: print("Greater than 10")

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct way to check if a variable 'var' is exactly equal to None in Python?

options: Using assignment operator instead of equality operator in the if condition.
Using a relational comparison between x and 10 is not allowed.
questions.correct_answer: Using assignment operator instead of equality operator in the if condition.
